business_problem: RingCentral needed a transcription platform that could handle hundreds of thousands of concurrent meeting users, different accents, specialized vocabulary, and noisy audio while still producing real-time results.
solution_summary: RingCentral modernized its transcription stack by taking pretrained NVIDIA speech models and adapting them with proprietary meeting data in NVIDIA NeMo, then deploying the resulting speech-recognition service with NVIDIA Riva for production use. NVIDIA DGX A100 systems provide the accelerated environment for training and experimentation, while NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supports scalable inference across large numbers of simultaneous audio streams. The end-to-end pipeline is built to handle diverse accents, domain-specific jargon, and noisy meeting conditions so transcripts arrive in real time and remain useful for downstream tasks. Those transcripts feed collaboration features such as live captioning, meeting summaries, and sentiment-oriented analysis, allowing RingCentral to support more than a billion meeting minutes without sacrificing speed or accuracy.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA NeMo

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Riva

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server

data_flow: Meeting audio is processed by NeMo-tuned ASR models trained on DGX A100 systems, Riva serves live transcription in production, and the resulting transcripts flow into captioning, summarization, and sentiment-analysis features.
integration_points: Sentiment analysis for video conferencing and call center sessions
business_outcome: RingCentral improved transcription accuracy by more than 10 percent, supported over a billion minutes of meetings for 200,000 concurrent users, and raised the quality of downstream summarization and sentiment-analysis tasks.
